# SyncStatus

One line that says where the person's changes are: Saved, Saving…, Offline (kept on this device) or Couldn't save, each with its icon, and Retry while there is a problem. Screen readers hear it only when a problem starts and when it clears, so every save is not narrated. It keeps the height of its longest state, so a change never moves the page.

```tsx
import { SyncStatus } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/sync-status/sync-status";
```

## Example

```tsx
<SyncStatus status={navigator.onLine ? (pending ? "saving" : "saved") : "offline"} onRetry={flush} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `toast()` instead to confirm a single action, and `Alert` for a problem that blocks the page.

## Props

Type: `SyncStatusProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, placement (`mt-3`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `labels` | `SyncStatusLabels` |  | The words for each state. |
| `onRetry` | `(() => void)` |  | Shows Retry while `offline` or `error`, and is called when it is pressed. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `status` (required) | `"error" \| "saved" \| "saving" \| "offline"` |  | `saved` once changes reached the server, `saving` while they travel, `offline` while they wait on this device, `error` when the server refused them. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `online`: Not a prop. Ouro UI says `status`: `<SyncStatus status="offline" />`.
- `state`: Not a prop. Ouro UI says `status`: `<SyncStatus status="saving" />`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `SyncStatusLabels`

The words for each state, for apps in other languages or to say what is saved.

```ts
interface SyncStatusLabels {
  /** Once changes reached the server. @default "Saved" */
  saved?: string | undefined;
  /** While changes travel. @default "Saving…" */
  saving?: string | undefined;
  /** While changes wait on this device. @default "Offline: changes are kept on this device" */
  offline?: string | undefined;
  /** When the server refused the changes. @default "Couldn't save" */
  error?: string | undefined;
  /** The retry button's label. @default "Retry" */
  retry?: string | undefined;
}
```
